target.title: fix(sessions): prevent delivery-mirror prompt contamination with adjacent dedup and identity fallback (#99470)
target.body:
Fixes #99470.

## What Problem This Solves

Channel-final delivery-mirror assistant entries leaked into model prompts as duplicate assistant messages. When session rebuild / side-branch merge stripped `provider`/`model` metadata from delivery-mirror entries, the existing `isTranscriptOnlyOpenClawAssistantMessage` filter (which keys exclusively on `provider="openclaw"` / `model="delivery-mirror"`) failed to recognize them. The result: the model saw adjacent byte-identical assistant pairs and occasionally mimicked the pattern — emitting the same answer twice inside a single completion.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two-layer fix:

1. **Identity fallback (Layer 2)**: `isTranscriptOnlyOpenClawAssistantMessage` now also checks for the `openclawDeliveryMirror` field. This field survives serialization even when rebuild/merge strips `provider`/`model`, so delivery-mirror entries are recognized as transcript-only regardless of metadata degradation.

2. **Adjacent duplicate collapse (Layer 1)**: `normalizeAssistantReplayContent` now drops an assistant message whose content is byte-identical to the immediately preceding assistant message when neither carries tool calls. This is defense-in-depth: even if a delivery-mirror entry's identity is lost through every available marker, the content-level dedup prevents it from reaching the model prompt. User turns reset adjacency; tool-call-bearing turns are never collapsed; empty-content messages (legitimate provider states) are preserved.

## User Impact

- Duplicate assistant history (~33% of prompts on busy sessions) is removed from model context, saving context-window tokens.
- ~2–5% of long replies no longer contain user-visible duplicated content.
- Delivery-mirror transcript receipts (persisted JSONL entries used for re-delivery idempotency) are unchanged — only the in-memory replay copy is cleaned.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: delivery-mirror entries with stripped `provider`/`model` survive the metadata-only filter and leak into model prompts; adjacent byte-identical assistant pairs are model-visible.

**Real environment tested**: Node 24.13+, local OpenClaw checkout.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```
node --import tsx -e "
import { isTranscriptOnlyOpenClawAssistantMessage } from './src/shared/transcript-only-openclaw-assistant.js';
const cases = [
  { label: 'intact delivery-mirror', msg: { role: 'assistant', provider: 'openclaw', model: 'delivery-mirror' } },
  { label: 'stripped mirror (openclawDeliveryMirror)', msg: { role: 'assistant', openclawDeliveryMirror: { kind: 'channel-final' } } },
  { label: 'real assistant (no metadata)', msg: { role: 'assistant', content: 'real reply', usage: { totalTokens: 100 } } },
];
for (const { label, msg } of cases) {
  console.log((isTranscriptOnlyOpenClawAssistantMessage(msg) ? 'FILTER' : 'KEEP') + ' | ' + label);
}
"
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```
FILTER | intact delivery-mirror
FILTER | stripped mirror (openclawDeliveryMirror)
KEEP | real assistant (no metadata)
```

Layer 2: `isTranscriptOnlyOpenClawAssistantMessage` now catches stripped-metadata delivery mirrors via the `openclawDeliveryMirror` field fallback. Real assistant messages without that marker are correctly preserved.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  35 passed (35)

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/shared/transcript-only-openclaw-assistant.ts
 (passed, exit 0)

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts
 (passed, exit 0)

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.test.ts
 (passed, exit 0)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/transcript.test.ts --run -- -t "delivery mirror|transcript mirror|normalizeAssistantReplayContent"
 Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  6 passed | 45 skipped (51)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts --run -- -t "delivery mirror|transcript mirror|normalizeAssistantReplayContent"
 Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  2 passed | 165 skipped (167)
```

**Observed result after fix**: 
- Delivery-mirror entries are recognized via two independent signals: `provider`/`model` and `openclawDeliveryMirror` field.
- Adjacent byte-identical no-tool assistant duplicates are collapsed before they reach the model.
- Real assistant replies, tool-call-bearing turns, user-separated duplicates, distinct content, and empty-content provider states are all correctly preserved.

**What was not tested**: Live Telegram E2E with a busy long-lived session going through rebuild cycles. The fix is verified at the transport normalization boundary — the exact point where mirrors survive the metadata filter — with focused regression coverage for both the identity fallback and the adjacent-dedup boundary.

## Regression Test Plan

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.test.ts --run` | 35 passed (35) |
| `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/shared/transcript-only-openclaw-assistant.ts` | passed |
| `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts` | passed |
| `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.test.ts` | passed |
| `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/transcript.test.ts --run -- -t "delivery mirror\|transcript mirror\|normalizeAssistantReplayContent"` | 6 passed (51) |
| `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts --run -- -t "delivery mirror\|transcript mirror\|normalizeAssistantReplayContent"` | 2 passed (167) |
| `git diff --check` | clean |

## Root Cause

In `isTranscriptOnlyOpenClawAssistantMessage` (`src/shared/transcript-only-openclaw-assistant.ts:17`), delivery-mirror identification keys exclusively on `provider`/`model` metadata. Session rebuild (`buildSuccessorEntries`) and side-branch merge (`mergePromptReleasedSessionEntries`) can re-materialize messages without `provider`/`model`, causing delivery-mirror entries to survive the filter. Only intact `provider="openclaw"` + `model="delivery-mirror"` metadata can identify a mirror; stripped-metadata survivors have no fallback signal and become indistinguishable from real assistant turns. The adjacent-duplicate pattern (real reply + byte-identical mirror) is unique to the mirror machinery — no legitimate model behavior produces it.
